description: Century Egg Congee, known as Pidan Zhou, is a quintessential Chinese comfort food. This savory rice porridge is simmered to a creamy perfection, often featuring tender pork and the distinct, rich flavor of century eggs. It is a deeply satisfying and nourishing dish, perfect for a comforting breakfast or a light meal.

instructions.title: Prepare the Rice
instructions.text: Thoroughly rinse 1 cup of jasmine rice under cold running water until the water runs clear. Optionally, soak the rice for 30 minutes to an hour for a creamier congee, then drain.

instructions.title: Prepare Pork and Century Eggs
instructions.text: If using pork, thinly slice or mince the pork tenderloin. Optionally, marinate it with 1 tablespoon soy sauce and 1 teaspoon cornstarch for 10 minutes. Peel and dice the century eggs into small pieces. Slice ginger into thin matchsticks and chop green onions for garnish.

instructions.title: Start the Congee Base
instructions.text: In a large pot, combine the rinsed rice with 8-10 cups of water or chicken broth and half of the julienned ginger. Bring it to a boil over high heat, then immediately reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Add Pork
instructions.text: After 30 minutes, the rice should have started to break down and thicken. Add the marinated pork slices or minced pork to the congee, stirring gently to separate the pieces. Continue to simmer for another 10-15 minutes, or until the pork is cooked through and the congee reaches your desired creamy consistency.

instructions.title: Incorporate Century Eggs
instructions.text: Stir in the diced century eggs and the remaining julienned ginger. Cook for another 5 minutes to allow the flavors to meld. The congee should be thick, creamy, and fragrant.

instructions.title: Season and Serve
instructions.text: Season the congee with salt and white pepper to taste. Ladle the hot congee into individual bowls. Garnish generously with chopped green onions and a drizzle of sesame oil. Serve immediately.

tips: For extra creamy congee, freeze the rice overnight before cooking. The freezing process breaks down the rice grains, leading to a silkier texture.
Adjust water quantity for desired congee consistency; some prefer it thicker, others thinner. Add more hot water or broth if it becomes too thick during cooking.
Serve immediately with a dash of white pepper and a drizzle of sesame oil for best flavor. A sprinkle of crispy fried shallots or a few drops of chili oil can also enhance the experience.
